name: XRP Ledger
executive_summary: The XRP Ledger has been running since 2012, designed from the start for fast, low-cost cross-border payments rather than general-purpose computing, and fourteen years later at the time of this scoring that focus shows up in a Real-World Utility score of 86 and a TradFi score of 71. Real-world payment usage and TradFi rail access carry the score, while a small, curated set of roughly 35 validators and token supply that was mostly pre-mined at launch hold it back. The AI score of 65 reflects a ledger with rich built-in payment features but no ability to deploy custom code on top of it, a limitation that's been in place since launch.

key_findings: XRP's score is carried by two strengths -- real-world payment usage (86) and regulated institutional access (81) -- and held back by two weaknesses: token supply that was mostly created and allocated at launch rather than mined over time (64), and a validator set that's curated by a small group rather than open to anyone (46).

XRP Ledger has published a detailed, four-phase plan for becoming quantum-resistant, targeting completion by 2028 -- a documented roadmap rather than a vague promise, though nothing on it has shipped yet.

TradFi Approved scores 81. US spot XRP ETFs held about $1.07 billion in November 2026, CME XRP futures have traded about $81 billion in cumulative volume, and Ripple's national trust bank charter received final approval from the OCC on October 26, 2026, bringing its RLUSD stablecoin's reserves under federal oversight. Only about 27% of RLUSD's roughly $2.9 billion supply sits on the XRP Ledger itself; the rest is on Ethereum.

Decentralization is a persistent weak point at 46. The list of roughly 35 validators trusted to secure the network is curated and permissioned -- new validators aren't automatically added, they're chosen -- though the operator base itself is genuinely diverse: exchanges, universities, and individuals across the list, with Ripple itself running only one of the 35 directly.

Privacy & Confidentiality scores 32 -- the ledger is fully transparent today, with no way to hide a transaction. A confidential-transfer feature (XLS-0096) shipped in the August 2026 software release and is in validator voting, but at about 19-21 of the 35 validators in November 2026 it remains well short of the 29 needed to activate, and it would only cover a newer token type called Multi-Purpose Tokens, not XRP itself.

binding_cap.short_note: Capped by Programmability Tier Partial -- rich native primitives but zero deployable custom logic on mainnet.

key_findings: XRP Ledger only partially passes our programmability check, and that's what caps the AI score at 65 even though the underlying categories average to about 70.4. The ledger has genuinely rich built-in financial features -- a native decentralized exchange, an automated market maker, escrow and now atomic batching -- but there's no way to deploy custom code on top of it. Two things that might look like exceptions don't count toward this: Hooks-style smart contracts live on a separate network, not this ledger, and the EVM-compatible sidechain has its own validators and its own security, so neither adds programmability to XRP Ledger itself.

Composability & Atomicity scores 64, up from 56. Atomic batching (BatchV1_1) went live on October 9, 2026 after an earlier version was withdrawn over a bug: up to eight transactions can now be bundled so they all succeed or all fail, and usage ramped quickly. It still combines only the ledger's built-in transaction types, since custom code isn't available.

Privacy & Confidentiality scores 48 on the AI axis. Every transaction is visible by default with no confidential compute or zero-knowledge option, so an agent can't hide amounts or transaction logic. Permissioned Domains can restrict who's allowed to act, but they don't hide what was done once someone's allowed.

XRP Ledger earns a full pass on our reliability check. In October 2026 some ledgers took up to about 50 seconds to close instead of the usual 3-5 seconds, but ledgers kept closing throughout and a configuration change fixed it within about two days -- a slowdown, priced lightly in Execution Layer, not a halt.

Economic Predictability is XRP Ledger's strongest category on the AI framework at 85. Transaction fees are fixed and near-zero, with no bidding war for space -- an agent can know its exact cost every time.

Agent Tooling scores 67. The XRPL AI Starter Kit, including x402 agent payments, launched in June 2026 and has since processed about 15.7 million agent payments across roughly 5,400 services, though their total dollar value remains small.

watch_items: The confidential-transfer feature (XLS-0096) is in validator voting at about 19-21 of 35 validators. It needs 29 sustained for 14 straight days to activate. If it does, it would raise the Privacy & Confidentiality score -- though it would still only cover the newer token type, not XRP itself.

A proposed smart-contract standard (XLS-0101) remains in development with no mainnet vote. If it ships, it would clear the programmability check, and the AI score would publish its uncapped figure (about 70) instead of 65.

The native lending protocol and single-asset vaults are in validator voting at about 24-25 of 35. Activation would add institutional credit products to the ledger and is a Real-World Utility candidate once used.
The CLARITY Act failed a Senate procedural vote in September 2026 and is stalled. Passage in a later Congress would move XRP's regulatory standing from agency guidance to statute.
Ripple's post-quantum roadmap targets hybrid signatures on its developer network in the second half of 2026 and native post-quantum signatures by 2028. Nothing is live on a public network yet.

tiles.fee_yield_note: Approximate: about 1,500 XRP burned per day (November 2026 estimate). All fees are burned; none are paid to holders.
